title: One constrained vector is a pure gauge compensator; the second vector copy leaves relative physical data

claim.statement: A single normalized SO(2,3) vector compensator has no local physical scalar modes: its four constraint tangents coincide exactly with the four broken gauge directions. The corrected second vector copy is not automatically gauge-redundant and requires a separate multiplicity constraint.
claim.significance: This avoids the unstable noncompact alignment potential while preserving a concrete MacDowell-Mansouri/Stelle-West gravity route.

interpretation: The norm constraint replaces radial potential stabilization, and unitary gauge removes all one-compensator Goldstone directions.
Two constrained vectors share the same gauge group, so their relative orientation cannot be completely gauged away.
Keeping Lorentz symmetry requires selecting one multiplicity combination as compensator and eliminating or algebraically aligning the orthogonal copy.
That multiplicity selection is new dynamical or constraint input not supplied by candidate 48.
falsifiers: A hidden gauge symmetry acting on the two-copy multiplicity space could remove the relative modes and would modify the count.
If the second vector is not an independent field but only a representation multiplicity, a precise field construction may avoid the pair problem.
Quantum consistency of the constraint and gauge fixing remains untested.
nextBranches: Search the corpus for an existing U(2) multiplicity gauge symmetry that could quotient the second vector copy.
Construct a Lagrange-multiplier constraint V2=c V1 and audit its gauge and constraint algebra.
Insert the single constrained compensator into the MacDowell-Mansouri action and verify linearized Einstein equations.
